title: III–V. Two parts of interpretation; subject, object, medium; the fit interpreter
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss: The former holds that interpreter's state; that latter, his habit. The subject stands as a fit interpreter, in whom two things come up for consideration: condition plus instruction. V. If these three stand rightly, interpretation cannot fail toward be just, plus that truth stands as dug from that deep. In explaining that sense three things stand as toward be observed: subject, object, plus medium. IV. 3:16). 15:4; 2 Tim. Use stands as what stands as understood mediately (Rom. 516). 6, p. Sense stands as that sentence which stands as immediately understood from that author through that text (Luther, Wittenberg ed., vol. Interpretation has two parts: that sense plus explanation belonging toward what stands as said, plus the use plus application toward dogmas belonging toward faith plus manners. III.
pass_b_english: III. Interpretation has two parts: the sense and explanation of what is said, and the use and application to dogmas of faith and manners. Sense is that sentence which is immediately understood from the author through the text (Luther, Wittenberg ed., vol. 6, p. 516). Use is what is understood mediately (Rom. 15:4; 2 Tim. 3:16).
IV. In explaining the sense three things are to be observed: subject, object, and medium. If these three stand rightly, interpretation cannot fail to be just, and the truth is dug from the deep.
V. The subject is a fit interpreter, in whom two things come up for consideration: condition and instruction. The former holds the interpreter's state; the latter, his habit.
source_text: III. Sunt autem interpretationis duae partes, sensus, dictorumque explicatio, et usus atque applicatio ad dogmata fidei et morum. Sensus est illa sententia, quae ab auctore per textum immediate intelligitur, teste Luthero tom.6. Witeb. p.516. Usus, quae mediate, Rom. 15.4. 2. Tim. 3.16. IV. In explicatione sensus tria observanda sunt: subjectum, objectum & medium. Quae tria si recte se habeant, fieri non potest, quin interpretatio sit justa & veritas e profundo eruatur. V. Subjectum est interpres idoneus, in quo duo consideranda veniunt, conditio & instructio. Illa statum interpretis, haec habitum continet.
